videos.title: How AI is breaking the internet (and what to do about it)
videos.focus: Expert analysis of AI crawling, publisher economics and proposed compensation mechanisms
videos.summary: Cloudflare chief Matthew Prince argues that AI crawlers weaken the advertising and referral economics that funded much of the open web. The full TED talk distinguishes training access from ordinary search traffic and proposes technical and market responses. Its April publication date and consecutive-day TED publisher exposure are disclosed as editorial advisories.
videos.why_it_matters: Publishers and platform teams can examine crawler permissions, referral losses and compensation proposals separately, then decide which evidence would justify access rules without treating one infrastructure executive’s preferred market design as neutral consensus.

videos.title: AI developers vs. the law
videos.focus: Independent reporting on negligence, strict liability, evidentiary burdens and legal accountability for AI-agent harms
videos.summary: Reuters examines who could be liable when an AI agent causes harm, contrasting negligence with strict-liability theories and testing both against autonomous hacking incidents. Legal scholars explain how evidence, reasonable precautions and open-weight modification complicate existing doctrine. The October 18 original date is disclosed, and proposed liability rules remain contested rather than settled law.
videos.why_it_matters: Product and governance teams can distinguish safety controls from legal conclusions, preserve testing and monitoring evidence, and identify who owns consequential agent actions before deployment instead of assuming autonomy eliminates organizational responsibility.
